# Gobstopper

> Gobstopper is a local proxy that keeps Claude Code and Codex requests under a token limit by summarizing older turns without a model call.

`gobstopper proxy` is a local proxy on 127.0.0.1:8260 that compacts live requests from Claude Code, Codex, and any agent that speaks Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Responses, or OpenAI Chat Completions with a custom provider address (opencode, Crush, Aider, Goose). Past a threshold (128,000 estimated tokens by default), each request keeps the system prompt, the first task, and the newest three turns word for word, and replaces older turns with one mechanical summary that drops tool results over 500 characters. The summary rule is ported from CliffCompaction (arXiv:2609.26779), whose authors report up to 50% lower cost at a bounded context on the models they tested; Gobstopper has not rerun those benchmarks. On Terminal-Bench 2.1 (September 27 and 28, 2026; one trial per arm; GLM 5.3 Flash; 45,000-token threshold), Gobstopper at its default tail resolved 61 of 89 tasks against 60 for Claude Code with no proxy, within noise, and sent 29% fewer provider-reported input tokens. If it cannot parse a request, hits an internal error, or the provider rejects the compacted request for a reason other than length, it sends the original; a length rejection gets a further compaction and a retry. It never changes session files. It has shipped since v0.3.1, and since v0.7.3 it keeps only the newest three turns verbatim by default. Direct provider-store edits and automatic provider compaction stay disabled.

For saved Claude Code and Codex sessions, Gobstopper previews what each strategy would cut and writes a smaller copy. It stores the original bytes in a local vault first, so you can search for a dropped record or restore the whole session.

When to use this site:
- Use gobstopper.sh to learn what Gobstopper does, which strategies it runs, and how to install it.
- Use /docs for the full reference: installation, the proxy, strategies, configuration, the watcher, hooks, the snapshot vault, and the MCP server.
- Use /docs/proxy to point Claude Code, Codex, or another agent at the proxy, choose its settings, and troubleshoot, diagnose, repair, or bypass the proxy service. Routing for opencode, Crush, Aider, and Goose is tested against synthetic histories, not live sessions.
- Use /methodology for the occupancy model behind the projections and what each strategy does.
- Use /benchmarks for a live Terminal-Bench 2.1 run of the request proxy, dated results, cohort sizes, limitations, and aggregate downloads.
- Use /compare/cliffcompaction to see how Gobstopper and its proxy compare with CliffCompaction, the API-proxy compactor, and what the cliff strategy does.
- Use /compare/claude-code-compact to see how Gobstopper compares with Claude Code's built-in /compact, which replaces session history with a model-written summary.
- Use /blog for longer posts on the Terminal-Bench result, how Gobstopper compacts Claude Code and Codex sessions, how its archive and edit limits are model-checked and proved, and how it reads token use through aicharts.

## Pages

- [Gobstopper](https://gobstopper.sh/): what Gobstopper does, how to install it, and what it will not do to a running session.
- [Gobstopper documentation](https://gobstopper.sh/docs): the README, with every command, strategy, and configuration setting it documents.
- [Route Claude Code and Codex through the proxy](https://gobstopper.sh/docs/proxy): per-agent setup, every proxy setting, how compaction works, estimate calibration, limits, a troubleshooting table, service diagnosis and repair, and launching with a direct fallback.
- [Gobstopper methodology](https://gobstopper.sh/methodology): the occupancy model, the strategies, and the limits of the published benchmarks.
- [Gobstopper benchmarks](https://gobstopper.sh/benchmarks): a live Terminal-Bench 2.1 run of the request proxy with three arms, offline replays of 729 archived sessions, request-proxy replays and one afternoon of live proxy counters, a synthetic snapshot-recovery study, and historical single-session resume trials.
- [Gobstopper compared with CliffCompaction](https://gobstopper.sh/compare/cliffcompaction): where each tool runs, what each keeps and drops, what each has measured, the seven ways gobstopper proxy departs from the reference, gobstopper proxy, which ports CliffCompaction's summary rule to the same three API dialects, and the cliff strategy for transcript copies.
- [Gobstopper compared with Claude Code /compact](https://gobstopper.sh/compare/claude-code-compact): preview and undo versus an in-place model-written summary, what happens to the original bytes, and how gobstopper proxy keeps a live session under its auto-compaction trigger.

## Blog

- [Gobstopper blog](https://gobstopper.sh/blog): every post, newest first. Atom feed at https://gobstopper.sh/blog/feed.xml.
- [Introducing Gobstopper](https://gobstopper.sh/blog/introducing-gobstopper): what Gobstopper does, in ten short beats: the proxy that trims a live session, smaller copies of saved sessions, the local archive that undoes them, one benchmark result and its limits.
- [Gobstopper on Terminal-Bench: fewer tokens, the same tasks solved](https://gobstopper.sh/blog/gobstopper-on-terminal-bench): on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (one trial per arm, 45,000-token threshold), Claude Code behind gobstopper proxy solved about as many tasks as without it (61 vs 60 of 89, within single-trial noise) and sent 29% fewer input tokens; how the proxy works and how to try it.
- [What Kani and Lean prove about Gobstopper's compaction](https://gobstopper.sh/blog/proofs-for-the-admission-math): what the Kani and Lean proofs cover and leave out.
- [How Gobstopper model-checks its archive against crashes](https://gobstopper.sh/blog/vault-models-that-fail-on-purpose): the TLA+ models, their broken copies, and the Hegel tests.
- [How Gobstopper uses aicharts to show token use across your agents](https://gobstopper.sh/blog/how-gobstopper-uses-aicharts): the installer adds aicharts, which keeps a daily record of your agents' token use on your computer; gobstopper usage reads it beside the proxy's own counts.
